kept.title: context-gate and ask-gate are twin abstain/ask-by-default gates with identical shipped thresholds
kept.summary: lib/context-gate.js (inject-vs-abstain) and lib/ask-gate.js (predict-vs-ask) share the SAME four-guard shape and calibrated DEFAULTS: cosThreshold 0.50, gapThreshold 0.25 (external-gap), marginThreshold 0.08, localityThreshold 2 (of 4 project-locality categories), requireEmpirical true. Both default to the safe action (abstain / ask) and only fire on a high-confidence, specific, project-local, empirical note match. Change one set of thresholds and you almost certainly want to change the other.

kept.title: external-gap, not cosine/margin, is the load-bearing discriminator; cosine floor was lowered 0.55->0.50
kept.summary: MiniLM pulls a tight cluster of topically-adjacent orchestrator notes into a 0.50-0.55 cosine band, so neither a raw cosine cut nor a top1-top2 margin cut separates a true positive from useless-but-topical matches. The discriminating signal is external-gap (fraction of the note's content tokens recurring in the task text): the one real positive measured externalGap 0.34 vs every topical negative <=0.17. The cosine floor was dropped from 0.55 to 0.50 because the only positive label (resolveOwner / note-mq7kyiir6sx) sat at top1=0.548, margin=0.017 and the old gate abstained and MISSED the win. Thresholds are calibrated on n=1 positive — provisional.

kept.title: Only EMPIRICAL project-local notes can fire the gates; general principles/best-practices are rejected by design
kept.summary: requireEmpirical and the projectLocality guard mean a note must be concrete project-local scar-tissue (a gotcha, a decision-with-reason, a root cause) to be injected or to predict a user preference. General PRINCIPLES ('always prefer X', 'best practice') deliberately do NOT qualify — the base model already knows them, so injecting them is pure overhead. A vague topical note will never clear the gate, which is why KB authoring guidance insists notes be written empirically and project-locally.

kept.title: Learned ask/edge classifiers run in SHADOW; live source flips heuristic->learned only via a one-way promotion
kept.summary: The hand-tuned heuristic is the live decider by default. A separately-trained logistic classifier (scripts/ask-clf-*) runs ALONGSIDE in shadow, writing shadow_decision/shadow_conf to .graph/ask-journal.jsonl as training signal WITHOUT deciding. lib/ask-promote.js runs a comparator each cycle and only flips .graph/ask-clf/mode.json from 'heuristic' to 'learned' (one-way, shadow->enforce) once the model beats the heuristic by a margin over a stable window. A missing model/mode file degrades to pure heuristic, so the gate stays usable offline. Same pattern mirrors edge-clf/mode.json.

kept.title: Abstain-by-default exists to avoid the 'over-deliberation tax' measured in bench/report-v2..v7
kept.summary: The gates default to abstain because the benchmark found that on self-solvable tasks every orchestrator-ON arm did MORE work than OFF — injecting context the model didn't need is not free: it pays consult-overhead C (cache cost to hold the graph) AND nudges the model into extra deliberation. The whole point of the context-need gate is to suppress that tax by injecting only on a confident empirical match. This is why 'predict by default / inject only when confident' is a hard project stance, not mere caution.
